summary.headline: JSW Cement Q4 FY26 operating EBITDA rose 46% YoY to INR365 crore (19.3% margin), helped by a one-time INR211 crore deferred tax benefit lifting PAT to INR362 crore.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 11% YoY to INR1,895 crore on 3.99 million tons of sales volume (+7%), with cement realisation up 4.8% QoQ to INR4,673/ton. Operating EBITDA reached INR916/ton, but GGBS volumes grew only 5.4% YoY due to a slag supply disruption at Dolvi and RMC site closures in Western India. The Nagaur (Rajasthan) plant began commercial operations on 30 March 2026, and management trimmed the Punjab plan in favour of a 2.5 MTPA grinding unit at Nagaur. April demand was soft, though management says volumes are recovering from mid-May.

segments.name: Cement
segments.commentary: Q4 volume 2.35 million tons (+12% YoY); realisation INR4,673/ton (+4.8% QoQ); trade mix 51% vs 47% in Q3; clinker-to-cement factor 51%. FY26 realisation INR4,667/ton.

segments.name: GGBS
segments.commentary: Q4 volume 1.57 million tons (+5.4% YoY) after about 1.2 lakh tons lost to Dolvi slag shortage and RMC closures; FY26 volume +12% YoY. Q4 realisation INR3,682/ton; FY26 INR3,683/ton.

segments.name: RMC
segments.commentary: Q4 RMC revenue INR184 crore; FY26 about INR574 crore.

segments.name: Nagaur, Rajasthan (new)
segments.commentary: 3.3 MTPA clinker and 2.5 MTPA grinding started commercial operations on 30 March 2026; Q4 revenue negligible. INR23 crore of North branding and manpower spend was expensed in Q4. Guided 50-60% utilisation for FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth guided at mid-to-high teens, excluding the North plant; management says it is on track.

Capex guided at about INR2,300 crore in FY27 and INR2,200 crore in FY28; about INR2,400 crore already spent at Nagaur against a total of about INR3,500 crore including the additional 1 MTPA grinding unit.

Cost savings programme: over 50% of target achieved; about INR100/ton more expected in FY27 and the balance in FY28 (power about INR69-70/ton, logistics about INR36/ton, premiumisation about INR4/ton for cement).

Nagaur grinding capacity to rise to 3.5 MTPA shortly, and to 6 MTPA after a new 2.5 MTPA unit (INR430 crore, commissioning by Q4 FY28). Company-wide grinding target of 46 MTPA and clinker of 13.04 MTPA; FY30 capacity target of about 43.5 MTPA intact.
FY27 tax rate assumed at 25% under the new regime; Rajasthan state capital subsidy of about INR50 crore plus electricity duty waiver expected.
GGBS volume guidance of about 6.5-7 million tons for FY27 maintained.
UAE grinding unit delayed about one month by the war; commissioning now expected by end-April 2027.
capex_capacity: Nagaur: additional 1 MTPA grinding and waste heat recovery system nearing commissioning in the next few months, taking grinding to 3.5 MTPA.
Board approved a further 2.5 MTPA grinding unit at Nagaur (INR430 crore, Q4 FY28), taking Nagaur grinding to 6 MTPA, which uses the full 3.3 MTPA clinker.
Punjab (Mansa) 2.75 MTPA replaced by 2.5 MTPA at Rajasthan; EC delays make a Punjab commissioning by FY28 unlikely. Second Rajasthan kiln line to be decided once EC is in place.
Limestone reserves over 600 million tonnes in 4 blocks; land and approvals in place for up to three 10,000 TPD lines.
Clinker: FY26 production 3.74 million tons at Nandyal and Shiva; Fujairah produced 0.62-0.69 million tons in Q4.
demand_pricing: Q4 industry growth in company markets 8% YoY versus company cement volume +12%, implying share gains.
April 2026 demand soft due to Middle East-driven inflation, labour shortage from state elections (Tamil Nadu, Kerala, West Bengal); management says May is recovering.
Western India RMC closures from pollution concerns (Mumbai, then Pune to end-April) are now resolved, per management.

Cement realisations rose across all regions in Q4; GGBS realisation roughly flat QoQ. Management says no windfall from steel price rises because slag is contract-priced (5-year contract from October 2024, price review every 2.5 years).
North dealer network: about 1,000 dealers, 25% exclusive and 75% multi-brand; JSW Steel dealer network not yet leveraged.
Premium product share about 52% of volume in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the industry demand outlook and the growth of JSW Cement in the new northern region?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 volume growth is guided at mid-to-high teens excluding the North; April was soft but May is normalising.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex guidance and spend at Nagaur to date?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex about INR2,300 crore and FY28 about INR2,200 crore; INR2,400 crore already spent at Nagaur against a total of about INR3,500 crore including the additional 1 MTPA grinding.

qa_highlights.question: Why was INR23 crore of North spend not capitalised, and is it one-time?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said branding and promotion spend cannot be capitalised under its accounting policy; it is a recurring cost, as hoardings need replacing every 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Where will clinker for Punjab come from, and what is the impact of the Punjab delay?
qa_highlights.answer: Punjab EC is delayed beyond FY28. Nagaur clinker (3.3 MTPA) is fully used by the 6 MTPA grinding plan, so a second Rajasthan kiln line will be considered once EC is in place.

qa_highlights.question: How much cost saving is realised, and what remains?
qa_highlights.answer: Over 50% of the INR400/ton programme has been achieved; around INR100/ton is expected in FY27 and the balance in FY28, at company level about INR50-75/ton each year.

qa_highlights.question: Will GGBS prices benefit from higher steel prices, and is the UAE unit supply sufficient?
qa_highlights.answer: No windfall expected since slag is contract-priced and freight from China is high. Clinker for Dolvi is secured until December at pre-war fixed prices; the JV sells about 1.5 million tons to the UAE grinding unit.

risks_watch: West Asia conflict: higher packing, imported fuel and petrol/diesel costs, and inflation affecting near-term demand.
Dolvi slag availability and the Western region RMC/pollution disruption, which affected GGBS in Q4; watch Q1 FY27 GGBS volume recovery.
Punjab EC delay (elections due February 2027) and the timing of a second Rajasthan kiln line.
Nagaur ramp-up: first month of operations; management will update on utilisation at end-Q1 against the 50-60% full-year guidance.
Ongoing rupee depreciation (INR13.4 crore hit in Q4) and the April-May demand softness.
Cost savings delivery: about INR100/ton still to come in FY27.
summary.management_tone: Confident on medium-term growth and the Nagaur launch, but cautious on April-May demand and the West Asia impact. Management was candid about the Dolvi slag and RMC disruptions and the Punjab delay, and was firm on guidance reconfirmations.
